case_name: Sayed Darain Ahsan @ Darain v State Of West Bengal & Anr.
facts: The facts briefly are that an FIR was lodged with the Officer-in-charge of the Garden Reach Police Station, Calcutta, on 11.02.2001 at about 10.18 P.M.
On 11.02.2001 at about 9.45 P.M., Md. Jahangir alias Mughal walked along Iron Gate Road towards Garden Reach Road
Rashid and Shamim and some people who had gathered from neighbouring areas took Mughal to Hannan Nursing Home at B-79, Iron Gate Road, where Mughal was declared dead.
After investigation, chargesheet was filed against the appellant and Abuzar Hossain under Section 302/34, IPC, and the case was committed to the Sessions Court for trial.
issues: The legal questions or points of law being debated
petitioner_arguments: The ocular evidence of PW-3, PW-4, PW-5 and PW-7 ought not to have been believed because it is inconsistent with the medical evidence in the present case.

These witnesses have said before the Court that the appellant and his associates surrounded the deceased and all of them fired at the deceased but the medical evidence reveals that there was only one bullet injury on deceased.
As per the Forensic Science Laboratory report dated 04.06.2001, the bullet fired was of a .303
respondent_arguments: All the eyewitnesses have named the appellant as the person who was holding a gun and who shot the deceased.
The contention of Mr. Sanyal that the report dated 04.06.2001 of the Forensic Science Laboratory was not put to the appellant in his examination under Section 313, Cr.P.C. is not correct.

There is no inconsistency between the ocular evidence and the medical evidence in this case and this Court should also accept the ocular evidence of the four eyewitnesses who had seen the appellant firing at the deceased.
court_reasoning: We may first deal with the arguments of Mr. Sanyal that the medical evidence in this case is such as to make the prosecution story as told by PW-3, PW-4, PW-5 and PW-7 improbable.

It will be clear from the evidence of PW-3, PW-4, PW-5 and PW-7 that the consistent version of all the four eyewitnesses is that the appellant and his associates fired at the deceased and as a result the deceased fell down.
holding: The final decision, order, or outcome
